text:
Alice: heads-up — CI is red on master: intermittent failure in runtime::serve::session_concurrency_test on linux-builder-7.
Ben: saw the CI job, retest didn't reproduce for me.
Alice: Pasted failing snippet from the Jenkins artifact:
```
FAIL runtime/serve/session_test.cc: line 312: expected 0, got 1
Thread 3: ASSERT lock order violated: mutex(session_map) -> mutex(connection)
stack: serve/session.cc:198 serve/connection.cc:76
```
Chloe: that looks like a classic lock-order inversion under stress; could be test scheduling dependent.
Ben: does the failure correlate with seed? any --runs_per_test or shuffle logs?
Alice: CI log shows: RUN_SEED=4829, runs_per_test=50. Locally I can repro with --runs_per_test=200 after a few minutes.
Chloe: Can you push a reproducer branch that runs the test under --run_under=tools/stress_runner ?
Alice: trying now — pushing @Ben for a quick review if I add a temporary deterministic scheduler fixture to force ordering.
Ben: I'd prefer to first try adding a small sleep between lock acquisitions to validate hypothesis, then follow with fixture.
ci-bot: Rebuild queued: https://ci.redwood.example/build/2149000000 (job id 8932)
Alice: ok test-run queued. If reproducible we can either: 1) make test deterministic, 2) add flake tag and track in flaky-tests board, or 3) change impl to avoid lock inversion.
Chloe: agree. If we opt for (1), please include a test-only strict-order fixture rather than sleeps.
Ben: also add a comment linking the issue: https://issues.redwood.company/INF-4122
Alice: thanks — will update PR with the reproducer log and plan. cc @Chloe @Ben :thumbsup:
